maya: Ran a longctx soak with INT8 enabled on prod-sim; after ~20k tokens memory climbs steadily, ~+2.1GB over baseline. attaching logs.
bench-bot: bench-ci: run 2026-03-17T22:14Z longctx-soak-042 -> p50 +3ms, mem +2.1GB :eyes:
arjun: Can you paste the KV stats (slab/pages/frag) from that run?
maya: ```
KV_STATS:
  slots_in_use: 124000
  pages_alloc: 3420
  frag_pct: 18.3
  int8_pages: 3100
  bf16_pages: 320
  kv_copy_backups: 1
```
liam: That's weird — int8_pages >> bf16_pages but traces show fallback to BF16 kernels fairly often?
sasha: I inspected the kernel selection trace. When a quant kernel hits a clamp/overflow it falls back to bf16 path and materializes an extra bf16 KV copy per layer.
maya: Trace snippet: ```
[layer 7] quant_kern: clamp_err at tok=18732 -> fallback:bfloat_kern alloc_bf16_kv +1.2MB
[layer 8] quant_kern: ok
[layer 9] quant_kern: clamp_err at tok=18735 -> fallback:bfloat_kern alloc_bf16_kv +1.1MB
```
arjun: So we're ending up with both int8 slot and bf16 slot sitting around until compaction runs? That would explain the growth.
liam: Compaction only runs on a per-request budget and our recent batching/coalescing change increases simultaneous unique keys, so compaction gets suppressed.
maya: :face_with_monocle: Could the batching heuristics be preventing compaction? We recently increased the coalescing window to improve throughput.
sasha: Exactly. Larger coalescing -> more concurrent hot references -> compaction heuristic treats slots as hot and avoids evict, so shadow bf16 copies accumulate.
arjun: Any dequant metrics?
maya: ```
DEQUANT_COUNTS:
  layer_fallbacks_total: 2184
  avg_dequant_size: 980KB
  compaction_runs: 4 (expected >20)
```
liam: Root cause looks like: quant instability + heuristic tweak => duplicated residency + slow compaction -> mem growth. Is there an accuracy regression?
maya: On eval set, INT8-only shows ~0.6% avg F1 delta. When fallback to bf16 happens the output aligns with bf16 baseline; so accuracy is OK when fallback occurs, cost is memory.
sasha: Risk: if growth continues we may hit host paging/eviction which will spike latency and potentially trigger further kernel fallbacks in a loop.
arjun: Immediate mitigation ideas: 1) reduce coalescing window in longctx mode 2) force-free the INT8 slot when a bf16 fallback is materialized 3) trigger an early compaction when shadow_pages > threshold
maya: I prototyped (2). Patch diff snippet: ```diff
- keep_int8_on_fallback = true
+ keep_int8_on_fallback = false
+ free_shadow_after_dequant()
```
bench-bot: perf-ci: PR 4892 with force-free patch -> longctx soak 1h: mem delta reduced to +120MB, p95 latency unchanged.
liam: Nice. Let's canary this on Dedicated. Also we need a CI soak that induces quant clamp to avoid regressions.
sasha: I'll add telemetry: emit kv.shadow_ratio and fallback_count/min. Also uploading flamegraphs to artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/test/4892/longctx-flame.html
maya: Owners + actions: maya opens canary PR, sasha adds metrics, arjun adds regression test. ETA: EOD tomorrow.
arjun: Ack. Also flagging kernel team to look at clamp frequency — maybe numeric tuning prevents the fallback churn.
bench-bot: Ticket PERF-1278 created for kernel numeric tuning.
maya: Thanks all — collecting logs/trace links in the ticket.
__notes: single-thread Slack export: messages are chronological, short informal replies, code blocks and links included per agents.md guidance
